idiom_name: AbstractCollection/AbstractList subclass + Collections.unmodifiableList (live view) or List.copyOf (snapshot)
implementation_notes: The JDK provides the skeleton: extend AbstractCollection (implement iterator and size) or AbstractList (implement get and size) and the framework supplies the rest of the Collection/List contract, including iterators and bulk operations, so only the domain methods and the validation are yours. Put validation in add/addAll and keep the backing ArrayList private. For reads, choose deliberately between the two exposures the JDK offers: Collections.unmodifiableList is a live read-only view - mutations made through the owner remain visible, and it is not an immutable collection - while List.copyOf/List.of return a truly immutable snapshot at the cost of one defensive copy. Implement equals/hashCode consciously if the collection is compared as a value: List semantics keep duplicates and order, Set semantics do not.
pitfalls: Collections.unmodifiableList is a view, not a copy: holders observe later mutations of the backing list, and the backing list itself stays writable from inside the class.
AbstractList's iterator supports remove()/set() through the list - an unvalidated mutation path that bypasses your invariants unless you override it or iterate over a snapshot.
Never return the internal ArrayList or a subList view of it: subList is a view whose set()/add() write through to the owner.
If you override addAll for performance, re-apply the invariants - the inherited implementation only loops over your validated add.
